concerns.location: tasks.md:T006 (src/metrics/correlation.py) vs constitution Principle VI and contracts/metric_results.schema.yaml
concerns.text: Constitution Principle VI mandates Fisher's z-transformed correlation deviations for every generator evaluation, and the metric-results schema defines a `fisher_z_deviation` field, but T006's correlation.py spec lists only 'Pearson and Spearman matrices ... absolute differences per pair, and a permutation-based correlation test'. No task produces fisher_z_deviation, so the schema field will be null everywhere and the constitution-mandated metric has no implementing work. Add Fisher's z computation to T006's deliverables and a test asserting non-null values for correlation entries.

T007 says 'replace a random subset of values in each column with draws from the empirical marginal distribution' but never specifies the subset fraction or replacement rule. An implementer cannot deterministically construct this control, and T008's marginal false-negative rate depends on it. Pin the fraction (e.g., 50% of rows per column) and the sampling procedure in the task text and metadata.

concerns.location: tasks.md:T008 vs plan.md Phase 5 and data-model.md §6
concerns.text: T008 assigns the correlation-perturbation control as ground truth for 'marginal false positives' and 'correlation false negatives', while plan.md Phase 5 and data-model.md §6 state the same control provides 'false-positive rates for correlation tests'. The artifacts assign opposite error-type semantics to the same control; an implementer cannot determine which FP/FN definitions T008's tests should encode. Reconcile the control-to-error-rate mapping across plan/data-model/tasks before execution.

T011 requires a rendered PDF but names no generation mechanism. data-model.md §7 says 'PDF generated from a Jinja2-rendered LaTeX template ... avoiding external LaTeX dependencies', which is internally contradictory (LaTeX rendering requires a LaTeX toolchain). Specify the concrete rendering path (e.g., reportlab or matplotlib PdfPages) so the pdfminer.six verification is executable.

'should any step inadvertently require CUDA, the execution engine auto-offloads to a free Kaggle GPU' contradicts FR-002's 'No GPU usage is permitted' and is not actionable by any task. Remove or reword to keep the CPU-only contract unambiguous.
